automation.title: Automation
automation.intro: Restart after a crash, actions at fixed times, backups with retention and restore, Discord notifications: the server looks after itself.
automation.restart_note: If the server exits without you stopping it, Mineger restarts it with growing waits (5 s, 15 s, 45 s, then 60 s). A stop from the app, a webhook or a schedule does not count as a crash.
automation.discord_note: A channel webhook, no bot and no token to keep: in Discord open Channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks, create one and copy its URL. If Discord does not answer, the server starts anyway.
automation.schedules_note: Start, stop, restart, back up or send a command at fixed times. Times are those of the PC hosting the server; runs missed while the app was closed are not caught up.
automation.command_placeholder: e.g. say The world is about to be saved
automation.backup_note: Every backup zips the world into backups/ inside the server folder. Retention and backup-on-stop apply to every backup, manual ones included.

server_off.title: Server is off
server_off.detail: The test from outside only makes sense with the server running.
server_off.detail_starting: The server is still starting: wait until it is online and try again.
server_off.fix: Start the server, wait until it is online and press the button again.

not_listening.title: The server does not answer even from here
not_listening.detail: No answer on {lan_ip}:{port} ({error}). The process is running but is not listening on this port or on this interface.
not_listening.fix: If it has just started, wait a few seconds. Otherwise check in Properties that server-ip is empty and server-port is {port}.

ok.title: Yes: friends can get in
ok.detail: From outside your home, port {port} answers on the public IP {public_ip} (tested by {via}, {latency} ms).
ok.fix: Give your friends this address. If your public IP changes (router reboot, new provider) the address changes with it: run the test again if they can no longer join.

tunnel_ok.title: Yes, through the tunnel
tunnel_ok.detail: Port {port} on the public IP does not answer, but the playit.gg tunnel does: friends get in with the tunnel address.
tunnel_ok.fix: Give your friends the tunnel address, pasted as it is.

wrong_target.title: The port answers, but it is not this server
wrong_target.detail: A different Minecraft server answers on {public_ip}:{port} (protocol {external_protocol} instead of {local_protocol}): the router's port forward points at another PC or another server.
wrong_target.fix: In the router panel, point port {port} at {lan_ip}, or use the tunnel.

cgnat.title: Your provider shares your IP (CGNAT): no port can be opened
cgnat.detail_cgnat: The router's WAN address is {wan}, in the provider's shared space (100.64.0.0/10): incoming connections stop before reaching your home, with or without a port forward.
cgnat.detail_private: The router's WAN address is {wan}, a private IP: there is another device in front (the provider's modem, or a double NAT), and incoming connections never arrive.
cgnat.detail_ds_lite: The router's WAN address is {wan} (DS-Lite): incoming IPv4 connections are impossible on this line.
cgnat.detail_upstream: The router's WAN IP ({wan}) is not the public IP seen from the Internet ({public_ip}): there is a provider NAT, or a VPN running on this PC, in between.
cgnat.detail_upnp: The router reports a private IP: incoming connections never reach your home.
cgnat.fix: Turn on the playit.gg tunnel: it works regardless. Otherwise ask your provider for a public IP: Fastweb gives one for free on request (192193 or social support), Iliad offers "IPv4 full stack" through customer service (or use a port in your assigned range, shown in the router panel), TIM and WindTre FWA on request.

firewall.title: Windows Firewall is blocking Java
firewall.detail_blocked: The port reaches the PC, but a rule blocks inbound {program} ({rule}): anyone trying to join times out.
firewall.detail_no_rule: The port reaches the PC, but no rule allows inbound {program} on the {profile} network profile: Windows drops the connections silently (this is what happens when the security alert is closed with Cancel).
firewall.fix: Press "Allow in the firewall": it adds a rule for Java on port {port} (Windows asks for administrator permission). Or Windows Settings → Firewall → Allow an app.

port_closed.title: Port {port} does not answer from outside
port_closed.detail_upnp_off: UPnP is off and the router is not forwarding port {port} to this PC.
port_closed.detail_upnp_failed: The router refused to open the port through UPnP ({message}).
port_closed.detail_upnp_pending: UPnP has not opened the port on the router yet.
port_closed.detail_upnp_open: The router says it opened the port, but from outside it does not answer: the provider may block incoming ports, or an antivirus has its own firewall.
port_closed.detail_forwarded: The router already manages port {port} with a rule of its own, but from outside it does not answer: check that it points at {lan_ip}.
port_closed.fix: Open the port by hand in the router panel: port {port} TCP to {lan_ip}. Or turn on the playit.gg tunnel, which needs no ports.
port_closed.fix_upnp_off: Turn on UPnP (the router opens the port by itself) or set up a port forward by hand: port {port} TCP to {lan_ip}. If that fails, the tunnel always works.
port_closed.fix_firewall_hint: Then allow Java in the Windows firewall too.

unknown.title: I could not test from outside
unknown.detail: The services that test from outside did not answer ({error}).{facts}
unknown.fix: Try again in a few seconds. With a VPN or a proxy on, the test can fail even when friends get in.
